Lessons.Title: Rigid Transformations in the Plane
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: Use coordinate differences to verify congruence and explicitly map vertices by translations, rotations and reflections.
For P,Q, d²=(x2−x1)²+(y2−y1)² Check squared distances before SSS Points (0,0),(3,4) distance 5
Translation adds v; reflection and rotation preserve distance Apply same map to all vertices Track labels and verify every length

Teacher rubric (0–8): four human-scored 0/1/2 criteria cover grid/Pythagoras original source A→B and exact figure uncertainty, two ordered transformations of Figure H with correct generic vertex maps, source ABC/DEF full side lengths and single90° centre(0,−2) congruence proof, and seven source Practice with teacher review of source figures and exact mathematics.
Source: Illustrative Mathematics Geometry First Edition (2019–2021), Unit 6 Lesson 1, CC BY 4.0. Independently authored Edulytiks examples, no copied figures/restricted assessments.

Source 1.1 Traversing the Plane (5 min): two source plotted points A and B require pupils to compute displacement by drawing horizontal and vertical RIGHT TRIANGLE and Pythagoras, then propose one or multiple rigid transformations A→B with directed segment language. The original marked coordinates are absent in accessible task text, so no invented distance or translation values. Teacher requires exact student diagrams and original figure. The distance between generic two labelled coordinates is sqrt((xB−xA)^2+(yB−yA)^2) because of a constructed right triangle; the source does not require rote memorization of standalone distance formula.

Source 1.2 Transforming with Coordinates (15 min): start with original source Figure H whose vertex coordinate labels only appear in figure, teacher supplies original H. For every generic vertex (x,y) first rotate CLOCKWISE90 about centre (2,0), mapping (x,y) to(2+y,2−x), then translate along directed segment from (2,0) to (3,−4) vector(1,−4), resulting R vertex (3+y,−2−x). Independently transform ORIGINAL H by reflection across y-axis (x,y)→(−x,y), then rotate COUNTERCLOCKWISE90 about origin→(−y,−x), resulting L. Students predict, plot, label, compare H,R,L, and write why all rigid-image trapezoids congruent despite changed orientation; distinguish rotate-after-reflect from reflect-after-rotate. No invented original H vertex list.

Source 1.3 Congruent by Coordinates (15 min): original labelled ABC vertices A(2,1), B(5,1), C(5,3); DEF vertices D(−3,0), E(−3,3), F(−5,3). Pythagorean side lengths AB3, BC2, ACsqrt13; DE3, EF2, DFsqrt13. Angles B and E are90; A=atan(2/3)≈33.690°, C≈56.310°, D=A, F=C; SAS/SSS shows ABC≅DEF with A↔D B↔E C↔F. A direct source-aligned SINGLE rigid transformation is counterclockwise90 about (0,−2), formula (x,y)→(−2−y,x−2), mapping A→D B→E C→F exactly. Alternatively CCW90 about origin followed by translation vector(−2,−2). Require teacher review of annotated drawing and full vertex/method argument; students revise proof with peers.

Source synthesis triangle END from original teacher figure is not fully labelled in activity text; one teacher example provides E'(−3,1),N'(3,−2),D'(3,−5) and a claimed translation from(−2,4) to(−3,1), vector(−1,−3), under original corresponding coordinates. Another teacher example E'(2,4),N'(−4,1),D'(−4,−2) with lengths EN sqrt45, DE sqrt72, ND3, proving SSS. Original source Lesson Summary independently illustrates triangle ABC=(1,1),(3,4),(2,4) and DEF=(−3,1),(−5,4),(−4,4), mapping via reflection y-axis then translate(−2,0). Preserve distinct summary example and actual 1.3 ABC/DEF values without conflating.

Source Practice P1-P7: P1 triangle ABC source picture only, reflect over line x=−3 gives (x,y)→(−6−x,y), then translate vector(4,1) yields (−2−x,y+1) applied to each actual source vertex; no fabricated final coordinates. P2 letter N rotated180 about centre of segment BC: in a symmetric block-letter capital N it can map onto itself, but original source exact segment labels/figure needed for unique statement. P3 ABC A(1,3),B(2,0),C(4,1) to A'(−5,−3),B'(−4,0),C'(−2,−1) is reflect across x-axis followed by translation(−6,0), equivalently y reflection then left6. P4 triangle ABC≅DEF original source image-only, teacher checks marked side/angle. P5 diamond pyramid base area2cm² height.5cm V=1/3 cm³, mass1.17g means density3.51g/cm³ > water1 so sinks under simplified rule. P6 oblique cylinder radius2 edge16 making30° to base: perpendicular height8, V=pi*(2)^2*8=32pi cubic units. P7 geometric rosette based on equilateral DEF and three equal circles: rotation120/240 about equilateral centre and reflections across axes through vertices, translation may show repeated motifs if suitably constructed; teacher uses original graphic before claiming exact three transformations. Original 1.4 A Transformed Triangle cooldown teacher-locked; first-party student paper coordinate grid, teacher rubric and fixture authoring.

Lessons.Title: Types of Transformations
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: Classify maps as rigid motions, nonrigid similarities, or neither based on whether distances are preserved or uniformly scaled.
Preserves all pairwise distances Test squared distance ratios=1 Reflection (x,y)→(−x,y)
Multiplies all distances by one k>0, preserves angles Uniform positive dilation k=2 Test independent direction lengths

Source activity parity: introduce the scale-3 coordinate map (x,y)↦(3x,3y) using a point B=(2,3), its image B′=(6,9), and auxiliary feet M=(2,0), N=(6,0). Students construct the two right triangles PMB and PNB′ and justify proportionality/angle agreement before classifying the map as a dilation. This independent reconstruction requires a genuine labelled coordinate diagram and teacher-reviewed reasoning.

Source-specific original activity: Sort coordinate-rule cards with explicit counterexamples; teacher checks written classification. Teacher rubric (0–4): correct geometric assumptions, accurate symbolic and diagrammatic representation, verified computations, and justified explanation. Student-produced diagrams and proofs require teacher scoring.
Source: Illustrative Mathematics Geometry First Edition (2019–2021), Unit 6 Lesson 3, CC BY 4.0. Independently authored Edulytiks examples, no copied figures/restricted assessments.

WorkedExamples.Title: Types of Transformations: justify scale three with auxiliary right triangles
WorkedExamples.Question: Point B=(2,3) maps to B′=(6,9). With origin P and feet M=(2,0), N=(6,0), explain why triangles PMB and PNB′ are similar and find PB:PB′.
WorkedExamples.Method: Compare corresponding right-angle legs and infer AA similarity for the origin-centred dilation.
Steps: PM=2, MB=3, PN=6, NB′=9; the horizontal and vertical leg pairs both have image/original ratio 3.
The triangles are right at M and N, and P,B,B′ lie on the same ray (both direction vectors are proportional), so their angles at P agree.
AA similarity gives PB′/PB=3 (or PB:PB′=1:3); independently PB=√13 and PB′=3√13.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Triangles PMB and PNB′ are similar by AA and PB:PB′=1:3.
WorkedExamples.Check: The coordinate map sends every vector from origin to three times itself and each leg scales exactly 3.
